mainTopic: Groups sharing a hall, brothers fed by their father, and which buildings in a courtyard count as a residence for עירוב.
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא of רבי יהודה הסבר. It says that בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that groups in a hall divided by partitions reaching the ceiling each need their own עירוב, and they argue only about partitions that stop short of the ceiling. The גמרא uses this ברייתא to refute some earlier views and support others, including the two versions of רב נחמן about a מסיפס. רב rules like רבי יהודה הסבר, and רב נחמן בר יצחק shows that the משנה's 'rooms and upper stories' means partitions reaching the ceiling. Two versions of a ברייתא then disagree about whether the dispute depends on the עירוב being placed elsewhere or coming to the groups. A new משנה teaches that brothers fed by their father but living in their own houses each need their own share, unless the עירוב is placed with them. The גמרא suggests that this proves the place where a person sleeps decides where he lives, and רב rejects that proof. Finally, a ברייתא debates whether storage buildings in a friend's courtyard block carrying, and רבי יהודה says only a real place of residence does. The amud ends as רב begins to define a 'מקום דירה', and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines exactly where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises an objection from רבי יהודה הסבר. Partitions that reach the ceiling need a separate עירוב for each group according to everyone. The מחלוקת is only about partitions that do not reach the ceiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raised an objection: רבי יהודה הסבר said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about partitions that reach the ceiling. In that case everyone agrees each group needs its own עירוב. What did they argue about? Partitions that do not reach the ceiling. בית שמאי say each group needs its own עירוב, and בית הלל say one עירוב is enough for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge some of the opinions it just discussed about what kind of divider the משנה means. This step only quotes the source; the next steps work out who it challenges and who it supports.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא draws a clear line between two cases. Partitions up to the ceiling turn each section into its own home, so everyone requires separate עירובין. Partitions that stop short of the ceiling are where בית הלל say the hall is still one home, so one עירוב is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא)
רבי יהודה 'the Keen', named for his sharp mind
Partitions that reach the ceiling
A shared food deposit that joins homes so people may carry between them on שבת
A group of people eating and staying together

steps.confusionAlert: Partitions that do not reach the ceiling are still real partitions. They are not the same as a מסיפס, which is a low divider made of pegs. This difference is the key to the later steps about רב נחמן.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Yehuda the Keen said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about partitions that reach the ceiling
that they require an eiruv for each and every group.
About what did they disagree?
about partitions that do not reach the ceiling,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: עֵירוּב לְכׇל חֲבוּרָה וַחֲבוּרָה,
phrases.english: for Beit Shammai say: an eiruv for each and every group,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: עֵירוּב אֶחָד לְכוּלָּן.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: one eiruv for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the opinions from the earlier part of the daf about which partitions the משנה means.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinions that place the מחלוקת in a case other than partitions that do not reach the ceiling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא openly says where the argument is (partitions below the ceiling) and where it is not (partitions up to the ceiling). Any opinion that places it elsewhere is contradicted.

steps.title: The ברייתא refutes one opinion and supports the other
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is a refutation (תיובתא) of the view that the argument is about partitions reaching the ceiling. It is support (סייעתא) for the view that the argument is about partitions not reaching the ceiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the one who said the argument is about partitions that reach the ceiling, this is a refutation. For the one who said the argument is about partitions that do not reach the ceiling, this is support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא scores the ברייתא against the two earlier opinions. One opinion loses and the other gains backing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that with partitions up to the ceiling, everyone requires separate עירובין, so nobody argues there. That directly contradicts the opinion placing the argument in that case. It matches the opinion that the argument is about lower partitions word for word.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the opinion is rejected
Support; a source that backs up an opinion
According to the one who said
A dispute

phrases.english: According to the one who said
the dispute is about partitions reaching the ceiling, it is a refutation,
and according to the one who said

phrases.aramaic: בִּמְחִיצוֹת שֶׁאֵין מַגִּיעוֹת לַתִּקְרָה מַחְלוֹקֶת — סִיַּיעְתָּא.
phrases.english: the dispute is about partitions not reaching the ceiling, it is support.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בִּמְחִיצוֹת הַמַּגִּיעוֹת לַתִּקְרָה מַחְלוֹקֶת תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from step 1 to the two earlier opinions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The view that the argument is about partitions up to the ceiling is rejected. The view that it is about partitions below the ceiling is supported.

steps.title: The first version of רב נחמן is refuted
steps.stepSummary: One version reports that רב נחמן said the argument is only about a מסיפס. The ברייתא refutes that version.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the version in which רב נחמן said the argument is about a מסיפס, this is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now checks the ברייתא against the first version of רב נחמן and concludes that this version is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version holds that only a weak divider like a מסיפס lets בית הלל require just one עירוב. With real partitions, it says, everyone would require separate עירובין. The ברייתא shows בית הלל require only one עירוב even with real partitions that stop below the ceiling, so this version cannot stand.

keyTerms.meaning: According to that version (of a reported statement)
רב נחמן, an אמורא
A low divider made of pegs or stakes, weaker than a real partition

phrases.english: According to that version in which Rav Nachman said:
the dispute is with a mesifas, it is a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהַךְ לִישָּׁנָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן מַחְלוֹקֶת בִּמְסִיפָס תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues scoring the ברייתא, now against the first version of רב נחמן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The version saying the מחלוקת applies only to a מסיפס is rejected.

steps.title: Is the second version of רב נחמן also refuted?
steps.stepSummary: Another version reports that רב נחמן said the argument applies even to a מסיפס. The ברייתא mentions only partitions, which might suggest that with a מסיפס everyone agrees. Does this refute that version too?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the version in which רב נחמן said the argument applies even to a מסיפס, shall we say this is a refutation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא might also refute the second version of רב נחמן. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the argument only with partitions. Someone could read this to mean that with a מסיפס there is no argument, and everyone agrees one עירוב is enough. If so, רב נחמן's claim that the argument covers a מסיפס too would be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Shall we say (a suggestion that the גמרא often rejects)
That it should be

phrases.english: According to that version in which Rav Nachman said:
the dispute is even with a mesifas,
shall we say it is a refutation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After refuting the first version, the גמרא tests the second version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רב נחמן: the argument applies even to a מסיפס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא places the argument only in partitions, which implies everyone agrees in the case of a מסיפס.

steps.title: רב נחמן answers: the ברייתא chose partitions to show how far בית הלל go
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן can answer that the argument applies to a מסיפס as well. The ברייתא mentions partitions only to show that בית הלל require one עירוב even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן could say to you: they argued about a partition, and the same is true about a מסיפס. The reason they argue about a partition is to show you how strong בית הלל's position is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the second version of רב נחמן. The ברייתא's silence about a מסיפס does not mean everyone agrees there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית הלל require only one עירוב even with real partitions, they surely do with a weak מסיפס. The ברייתא chose the harder case to show the full reach of בית הלל's leniency (כחן דבית הלל). So the argument covers both cases, and the second version of רב נחמן stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense on someone's behalf)
They disagree
And the same law applies
To show you the strength (far-reaching nature) of their view

steps.whatToRemember: Outcome: the argument is about partitions that do not reach the ceiling. With full partitions, everyone requires separate עירובין. The first version of רב נחמן (only a מסיפס) is refuted. The second version (even a מסיפס) survives, because the ברייתא mentioned partitions only to show the strength of בית הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step uses a common גמרא pattern: a source states the bolder case to show how far an opinion reaches, and the easier case is understood automatically.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman could say to you:
They disagree about a partition,
and the same is true of a mesifas.
And the fact that they disagree about a partition
is to show you the strength of Beit Hillel's view.
phrases.notes: בית הלל require one עירוב even with real partitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the source chose its case: to show the strength of בית הלל's view (להודיעך כחן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ברייתא mentions only partitions, with a מסיפס everyone would agree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument applies to a מסיפס as well. Partitions were mentioned to show that בית הלל are lenient even in the harder case.

steps.title: Why not set the dispute in a case of a light divider to show how strict בית שמאי are?
steps.stepSummary: If the dispute also applies to a מסיפס, the ברייתא should have used that case. It would show that בית שמאי are strict even there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them argue about a מסיפס. That would teach you how far בית שמאי's strictness goes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps pushing on the version of רב נחמן that says the dispute applies even to a מסיפס. It asks why the ברייתא did not pick that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 we said the ברייתא chose partitions to show how far בית הלל's leniency goes. The גמרא now asks: why not pick the מסיפס case instead? That case would show the opposite extreme, that בית שמאי are strict even when the divider is very light.

keyTerms.meaning: A low or light divider, such as a row of pegs or a small wall, that does not reach the ceiling
To teach you how far their view goes (the 'strength' of their position)
Let them argue

phrases.english: So let them argue about a light divider
phrases.notes: Meaning the ברייתא should have set the dispute in this case.

phrases.english: to teach you the strength of Beit Shammai!
phrases.notes: This would show that they require separate contributions even with a flimsy divider.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיפְלְגִי בִּמְסִיפָס לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחָן דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5 by suggesting a better way the ברייתא could have been written.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא chose partitions on purpose
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both cases are in dispute, the מסיפס case is just as useful to teach, because it shows how strict בית שמאי are. So why choose partitions?

steps.title: Showing the strength of a lenient view is preferred
steps.stepSummary: A תנא prefers to set a dispute in a case that shows how far the lenient side goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Showing the strength of a lenient ruling is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא deliberately chose the case that highlights בית הלל's leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A strict view can come from simple doubt or caution. A lenient view shows real confidence in the law. So when a תנא has a choice, he picks the case that shows how far the lenient side, here בית הלל, is willing to go.

keyTerms.meaning: Showing the strength of a lenient position is preferable
Leniency, a permitting ruling

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule found throughout ש״ס for explaining why a תנא chose one case over another.

phrases.english: The strength of a permissive ruling is preferable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule of how a תנא chooses which case to teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מסיפס case would be an equally good or better way to present the dispute.
steps.terutzMaskana: Highlighting the lenient view is preferred, so the ברייתא used partitions to show how lenient בית הלל are. The version of רב נחמן that includes a מסיפס stands.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה הסבר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רב, rules like רבי יהודה הסבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה הסבר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the dispute about how to understand the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה הסבר said that with partitions reaching the ceiling, everyone requires a separate עירוב for each group. The argument is only about partitions that do not reach the ceiling. That approach is now the accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law
רבי יהודה 'the Keen' (the sharp-minded), the תנא of the ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law. Partitions reaching the ceiling turn a hall into separate units that each need their own עירוב.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda the Keen.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַסַּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from analyzing the versions to the practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With partitions reaching the ceiling, everyone requires a separate עירוב for each group. The dispute is only about partitions that do not reach the ceiling.

steps.title: The משנה's wording also supports this ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the משנה supports רבי יהודה הסבר. He quotes the line where בית הלל agree that groups in rooms and upper stories need separate עירובין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: our משנה also shows this. It teaches that בית הלל agree that when some of the people live in rooms or upper stories, each group needs its own עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the ruling from the wording of the משנה. This step quotes the line that the next steps will analyze closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on the words 'rooms' and 'upper stories.' This step only presents the quote. The actual reasoning comes in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording of our משנה also points to this
And they agree (בית הלל concede)
A group of people eating or living together
Upper stories, attic rooms

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The mishna is also precise this way,
as it teaches: And they agree
that when some of them reside
in rooms or upper stories,
they need an eiruv
for each and every group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual support for the ruling of step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that follows רבי יהודה הסבר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'ומודים בזמן שמקצתן שרויין בחדרים ובעליות'

steps.title: What do 'rooms' and 'upper stories' mean? Literal rooms would be obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words mean. It rejects the literal reading because it would teach something obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are 'rooms,' and what are 'upper stories'? If you say they are real rooms and real upper stories, that is obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא examines the wording of the משנה. It rules out the simple meaning so that the true meaning can come out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real, separate rooms obviously need their own עירוב. That is the basic law of several households sharing a courtyard. A משנה would not need to say that בית הלל 'agree' to something so obvious. So the words must mean something less obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a reading about to be rejected)
Actual, literal
It is obvious (so why teach it?)

phrases.english: What are 'rooms,' and what are 'upper stories'?
If you say rooms means actual rooms,
and upper stories means actual upper stories,
that is obvious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the quoted words to build the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'rooms' and 'upper stories' in the משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not literal rooms, because that would be obvious. The answer comes in the next step.

steps.title: They mean areas like rooms: partitions that reach the ceiling
steps.stepSummary: The words mean spaces that are like rooms, which are areas closed off by partitions reaching the ceiling. This proves the view of רבי יהודה הסבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean 'like rooms' and 'like upper stories'? And what are those? Partitions that reach the ceiling. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The משנה is talking about partitions reaching the ceiling, and there בית הלל agree that separate עירובין are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Partitions that reach the ceiling make an area count like a room, even inside one hall. Since בית הלל agree in that case, the משנה matches רבי יהודה הסבר. Everyone agrees about partitions that reach the ceiling, and the argument is only about lower partitions.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, like
Partitions that reach the ceiling
Learn from this (the proof stands)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה הסבר. Partitions reaching the ceiling count like separate rooms, so everyone requires a separate עירוב for each group. The משנה's 'rooms and upper stories' refers to this case.

phrases.english: Rather, doesn't it mean: like rooms,
like upper stories?
And what are they?
Partitions that reach the ceiling.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו כְּעֵין חֲדָרִים כְּעֵין עֲלִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading after the literal reading was rejected, completing the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה refers to partitions reaching the ceiling. There בית הלל agree that separate עירובין are needed, which supports רבי יהודה הסבר.

steps.title: בית שמאי's strictness applies only when the עירוב is placed elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא limits the dispute. Separate contributions are needed only when the groups send their עירוב to another house. If the עירוב is placed in their hall, everyone agrees one is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: when does this apply? When they bring their עירוב to another place. But if the עירוב comes to them, everyone agrees that one עירוב works for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that sets a limit on when בית שמאי require a separate עירוב for each group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the groups must send a contribution to a different house, בית שמאי treat each group as its own household. But if the whole courtyard's עירוב is placed in their hall, they all live in the house where the עירוב rests. That joins them into one unit, so a single contribution covers everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught (in a ברייתא)
In what case was this said? (introduces a limit)
They bring or carry (to another place)
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא does not cancel בית שמאי's view. It only limits when that view applies, which is when the עירוב is placed in a different house.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute about separate contributions applies only when the עירוב is placed in another house. If it is placed in the groups' own hall, one contribution covers all of them according to everyone.

phrases.english: It was taught: in what case was this said?
When they bring their eiruv
to another place.
But if
their eiruv came to them,
all agree
that one eiruv suffices for all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים כְּשֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין אֶת עֵירוּבָן לְמָקוֹם אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new limit on the scope of the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי require separate contributions only when the עירוב is placed elsewhere. If it is placed in the groups' own hall, everyone agrees one contribution suffices.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא of the five who collected their עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view a ברייתא follows. The ברייתא says five who collected their עירוב and send it to another place need only one share for all of them. Answer: בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches this ברייתא? 'Five people who collected their עירוב: when they bring their עירוב to another place, one עירוב is enough for all of them.' Whose view is this? בית הלל's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and asks which side of the dispute it matches. It answers right away: בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the argument only happens when the group sends its עירוב to another house. בית שמאי require a share from each group there, and בית הלל say one share is enough. This ברייתא is exactly that case and says one share is enough, so it must follow בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does this follow?
That which was taught in a ברייתא
Who collected (pooled their food together)
Another place, meaning a different house in the courtyard
In line with the view of בית הלל

phrases.english: Whose view does that which was taught follow?
Five who collected their eiruv,
when they bring their eiruv to another place —
one eiruv suffices for all of them.
Whose view? That of Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the limit from Step 12 to identify who authored another ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the dispute the ברייתא of the five follows.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית הלל, because the dispute is about sending the עירוב elsewhere, and one share being enough is בית הלל's position.

steps.title: A second version that flips the limit of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: Some report the limit the opposite way. בית הלל allow one share only when the עירוב comes to the group. If the group sends its עירוב to another place, everyone agrees each group needs its own share.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: when is this said (that בית הלל allow one עירוב)? When the עירוב was coming to them. But if they were bringing their עירוב to another place, everyone agrees each group needs its own share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version (איכא דאמרי) of Step 12's limit, which reverses which case is debated and which is agreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, everyone agrees on the case where the עירוב is placed with the group, and they argue when it is sent elsewhere. In this version, they argue when the עירוב comes to the group, and everyone agrees that sending it elsewhere requires a share from each group. This switch sets up a problem for the ברייתא from Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (a second version of the passage)
In what case is this said? (introduces a limit)
Comes to them, meaning the עירוב is placed where they live
All agree
A group of people living together

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that disagrees with Step 12. It is a different report of the same teaching, with the two cases swapped.

phrases.english: And some say:
In what case are these words said?
When the eiruv was coming to them.
But if they were bringing
their eiruv to another place —
all agree they need an eiruv
for each and every group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing version of Step 12's limit, which removes the basis for Step 13's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, the dispute is only when the עירוב comes to the group. Sending it elsewhere requires a share from each group according to everyone.

steps.title: Under the second version the ברייתא fits no one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again whose view the ברייתא of the five follows. Under the second version, the answer is: no one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches this ברייתא? 'Five who collected their עירוב: when they bring their עירוב to another place, one עירוב is enough for all of them.' Whose view? Not anyone's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the exact question from Step 13. This time it answers that the ברייתא matches neither בית שמאי nor בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the second version, everyone agrees that sending the עירוב elsewhere needs a share from each group. A ברייתא that allows one share in that very case therefore fits neither side. The גמרא simply records this and does not try to fix it.

keyTerms.meaning: Five (people or groups sharing living space)
They bring or send
Not like anyone, matching neither opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The two versions disagree about which case the dispute covers. Under version one, the ברייתא of the five follows בית הלל. Under version two, it follows no one.

phrases.english: Whose view does that which was taught follow?
Five who collected their eiruv,
when they bring their eiruv to another place —
one eiruv suffices for all of them,
Whose view? Not in accordance with any one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of Step 14's version for the ברייתא from Step 13. The repetition of the text is deliberate.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose view the ברייתא follows under the second version.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No one's, because under this version all agree that sending the עירוב elsewhere needs a share from each group.

steps.title: משנה: brothers eating at their father's table but sleeping at home
steps.stepSummary: Brothers who eat at their father's table but sleep in their own houses in the same courtyard each need their own share in the עירוב. If one forgot, he must give up his rights in the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Brothers who eat at their father's table but sleep in their own houses each need their own share in the עירוב. Therefore, if one of them forgot and did not join the עירוב, he must give up his rights in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that each brother counts as his own household, so each must join the עירוב on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the brothers are fed by their father, the משנה treats each one as a separate resident of the courtyard, so each must contribute his own share. Why they count as separate is taken up in the גמרא: step 18 suggests it is because each sleeps in his own house, and step 19 rejects that. Since a brother who forgot would forbid everyone else from carrying, he fixes this by giving up his rights (ביטול רשות).

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Their father's table, where they eat
Sleeping in their own houses
Therefore
He renounces his rights in the courtyard

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude from this משנה that where you sleep decides where you live. The גמרא tries that inference in step 18, and רב rejects it in step 19: the brothers really take food portions from their father and eat them in their own homes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next discussion about what makes someone part of another person's household for עירוב purposes.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The brothers who were eating
at their father's table
and sleeping in their own houses —
need an eiruv for each and every one.
Therefore, if one of them forgot
and did not join the eiruv —
he renounces his rights.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאַחִין שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלִין עַל שֻׁלְחָן אֲבִיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה with a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers who sleep in their own houses each need their own share in the עירוב. One who forgot must perform ביטול רשות.

steps.title: When the brothers need separate shares
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits its ruling. The brothers need separate shares only when the עירוב is placed somewhere else. If the עירוב is placed with them, or no outside residents live in the courtyard, they do not need to make an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this true? Only when they bring their עירוב to another place. But if the עירוב comes to them, or if no other residents live with them in the courtyard, they do not need to make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the brothers' case from step 16 by saying exactly when each brother needs his own share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the עירוב is placed in the father's house, the brothers are treated as part of his household, so they do not need separate shares. If no one outside the family lives in the courtyard, they count like one person living there alone, so there is no one to make an עירוב with.

keyTerms.meaning: When? (a word that limits a rule)
They bring their עירוב to someone else's house
Residents, other people living in the courtyard
To make an עירוב

phrases.english: When is this so?
When they bring their eruv to another place.
phrases.notes: Another place means the house of a different resident of the courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה עֵירוּב בָּא אֶצְלָן,
phrases.english: But if the eruv was coming to them,
phrases.notes: This means the עירוב is placed in the father's house.

phrases.english: or if there are no residents with them in the courtyard,
they do not need to make an eruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין עֵירוּבָן בִּמְקוֹם אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling about the brothers in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separate shares are needed only when the עירוב is placed elsewhere. If it is placed with the family, or no outside residents live in the courtyard, no separate shares are needed.

steps.title: The place where you sleep seems to make it your home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that the place where a person sleeps decides where he lives.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We can learn from this that the place where a person sleeps is what decides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a general rule from the משנה. This also sets up the next step, where the rule is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers eat with their father but still need their own shares, because they sleep in their own houses. So it looks like sleeping, not eating, decides where a person lives for עירוב purposes.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (an inference)
The place where one sleeps
Determines, is the deciding factor

phrases.english: Gemara
Learn from it
that the place of sleeping determines one's residence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from the משנה's case of the brothers.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that sleeping, not eating, decides where a person lives.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that brothers who eat with their father but sleep at home need separate shares.

steps.title: רב: the brothers only receive food from their father
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, rejects the inference. The משנה is about brothers who receive a food portion from their father and eat it in their own houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: The משנה was taught about brothers who receive a portion of food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב pushes back the inference from step 18 by explaining what the משנה's case really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers do not actually eat at their father's table. They take their food from him and eat it at home. They need separate shares because of where they eat, so nothing can be learned about sleeping.

keyTerms.meaning: People who receive a food portion from someone else
They taught (this ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the brothers sit at their father's table. According to רב, they only get their food from him and eat it in their own homes.
steps.whyThisMatters: After this answer, there is still no proof that sleeping decides where a person lives. Eating can still be the key factor.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
They taught this about people who receive a food portion.
phrases.notes: They eat that portion in their own houses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בִּמְקַבְּלֵי פְרָס שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole inference that sleeping decides where a person lives.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference assumed the brothers eat at their father's table. In fact, they eat their portions in their own homes.

steps.title: Which buildings in a friend's courtyard block carrying
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that owning a gatehouse, porch, or balcony in a friend's courtyard does not block carrying. Owning a straw room, cattle shed, woodshed, or storehouse there does block it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone owns a gatehouse, porch, or balcony in his friend's courtyard, he does not make carrying forbidden for his friend. If he owns a straw room, cattle shed, woodshed, or storehouse there, he does make carrying forbidden for his friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about which kinds of buildings count as a 'home' for עירוב rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gatehouses, porches, and balconies are just passageways or open spaces. Nobody lives there, so they do not block carrying. Storage buildings hold a person's belongings, and the תנא קמא treats them as a residence, so they do block carrying until an עירוב is made.

keyTerms.meaning: Gatehouse
Porch, a roofed area that is open on the sides
Balcony
Makes carrying forbidden (without an עירוב)
Storehouse

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּית שַׁעַר, אַכְסַדְרָה, וּמִרְפֶּסֶת
phrases.english: One who has a gatehouse, porch, or balcony
in his friend's courtyard
does not make carrying forbidden for him.
But a straw room or a cattle shed,
a woodshed or a storehouse,
does make carrying forbidden for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּית שַׁעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: which kinds of buildings count as a residence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Passageways and open structures do not block carrying. Storage buildings do block carrying.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only a real living space blocks carrying
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees with the תנא קמא. Only a place where a person actually lives blocks carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Only a place where someone lives makes carrying forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the other side of the dispute in the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, storage buildings do not count, because no one lives in them. The disagreement is over whether 'residence' means only a living space, or also storage space.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where someone actually lives
Only

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says storage buildings block carrying. רבי יהודה says only real living spaces block carrying.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר אֶלָּא מְקוֹם דִּירָה בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: Only a place of dwelling makes carrying forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר אֶלָּא מְקוֹם דִּירָה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling about storage buildings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a living space blocks carrying. Storage buildings do not.

steps.title: The case of בן נפחא in אושא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה supports his view with a real case. בן נפחא had houses in five courtyards in אושא, and the חכמים ruled that only his living house blocks carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was a case with בן נפחא, who had houses in five courtyards in אושא. The case came before the חכמים, and they said: Only a house where he lives makes carrying forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה brings a story as proof for what he said in step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן נפחא actually lived in only one of the five houses. The חכמים ruled that the other four did not block carrying in their courtyards. This shows that a building a person owns but does not live in does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case or incident
A house a person lives in
אושא, a town in the Galilee

steps.whatToRemember: The story of בן נפחא is רבי יהודה's proof that only an actual home blocks carrying.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with ben Nappacha
who had houses in five courtyards in Usha,
phrases.notes: He lived in only one of them.

phrases.english: and the case came before the Sages,
and they said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ אוֹסֵר אֶלָּא בֵּית דִּירָה בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: Only a house of dwelling makes carrying forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּבֶן נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהודה's view from step 21 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's rule that only a living space blocks carrying.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of the חכמים in the case of בן נפחא in אושא.

steps.title: The wording 'house of residence' cannot be right
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the phrase 'בית דירה' in the ruling about בן נפחא. All five of his places were houses, so this wording cannot tell them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think the ruling said 'a house of residence'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ruling from the story of בן נפחא. It says 'בית דירה' makes no sense here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן נפחא owned a house in each of five courtyards. If the חכמים had said 'only his בית דירה blocks carrying', every one of those houses would qualify, and the ruling would not single out any one of them. So the wording must be a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: A house of residence; a living house
Would it enter your mind? (a sign that the wording cannot be right)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to רבי יהודה's ruling itself. The גמרא is only attacking how the ruling is worded. The הלכה stays the same.

phrases.english: Would it enter your mind that it says 'a house of residence'?
phrases.notes: He had houses in all five courtyards, so this wording points to nothing specific.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the exact wording of the ruling in the בן נפחא story from Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'בית דירה' in the ruling about בן נפחא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All five of his places were houses. 'House of residence' therefore cannot pick out one of them as the place that blocks carrying.

steps.title: Correct the wording to 'place of residence'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the text so it reads 'מקום דירה', meaning the place where he actually lives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: 'a place of residence.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge by changing one word in the ruling. It now reads 'מקום דירה' instead of 'בית דירה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Owning a house is not enough. What blocks carrying is the one place where בן נפחא actually lives day to day. In his other four courtyards he owns houses but does not live in them, so they do not block carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (a way of correcting the text)
The place where a person actually lives

steps.whyThisMatters: This sharpens רבי יהודה's view. What counts is actually living somewhere, not owning a building. That sets up the next question: what exactly makes a place your 'place of residence'?

phrases.english: Rather, say: 'a place of residence.'
phrases.notes: Only the place where he actually lives blocks carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording problem raised in Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to say that any 'house of residence' blocks carrying, and that wording fits all five houses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling means the one 'place of residence' where he actually lives. Only that place blocks carrying.

steps.title: What counts as a place of residence?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we define a person's 'מקום דירה' and begins to bring רב's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a 'place of residence'? רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what makes a place count as where someone lives. This step sets up the next move: רב's answer, which comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the rule depends on a 'מקום דירה', we need a clear test. Is it where he sleeps, where he eats, or something else? The words 'רב אמר' open the answer, which continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? (asking for a definition)
רב said (introduces his answer)

phrases.english: What is 'a place of residence'?
Rav said:
phrases.notes: This opens רב's answer. The answer itself comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the term 'מקום דירה' has been set in Step 24, the גמרא asks for its definition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The test for what counts as a person's 'מקום דירה' for blocking carrying in a courtyard.
